title: A NOX2-independent mechanism of Hv(1) channel activation promotes inflammatory cytokine release from BV-2 microglia via intracellular Ca(2+) mobilisation.
authors: Sharma, Ashutosh; Yadav, Priyanka; Yadav, Shivani; Kumar, Vikash; Ravendra Singh, Kunvar; Ranawat, Madhavi; Pal, Shivani; Yadav, Ankita; Nagendran, Gokul Krishnan; Kase, Sunil P; Yadav, Yaduvender; Mudedla, Satish K; Shinde, Valmik S; Kshatri, Aravind Singh
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子激活Hv(1)质子通道引发小胶质细胞炎症的机制，虽用分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Microglia are the primary immune cells to sense and respond to all the pathological events in the brain. Voltage-gated proton channels (Hv(1)) are specifically expressed in the microglia to regulate their intracellular pH and contribute to redox homeostasis. Our previous work identified that S-023-0515 is a novel activator of microglial Hv(1) channels, inducing neuroinflammation through unknown mechanisms. In this study, we demonstrate the direct binding of S-023-0515 onto the Hv(1) channel using molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) techniques. Treatment with S-023-0515 induced a sustained intracellular alkalization, resulting in a gradual increase in cytosolic Ca(2+) levels. None of the major plasma membrane Ca(2+) ion channels, such as TRPV1, Cav1.2, ASIC and P2X7, nor intracellular Ca(2+) release channels were found to be involved in S-023-0515-induced Ca(2+) increase. This mobilisation of Ca(2+) occurred through the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+)-ATPase (SERCA), as its inhibition annulled the S-023-0515-mediated Ca(2+) rise. Hv(1)-mediated Ca(2)(+) signaling further promoted NF-kappaB activation leading to a steady increase in proinflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-alpha and IL-1beta, in BV-2 microglial cells, representing an inflammatory microglial phenotype. Notably, the proinflammatory response was solely attributable to Hv(1) channel activation because neither NOX2 stimulation nor local cellular pH was altered following S-023-0515 treatment. Together, these findings suggest that NOX2-independent activation of Hv(1) channels triggers a Hv(1)-SERCA-Ca(2+)-NF-kappaBeta signalling cascade, disrupting intracellular Ca(2+) homeostasis and leading to microglial neurotoxicity.
abstract_zh: 小胶质细胞是大脑中感知和响应所有病理事件的主要免疫细胞。电压门控质子通道（Hv(1)）特异性地表达于小胶质细胞中，以调节其细胞内pH值并参与氧化还原稳态。我们先前的研究确定S-023-0515是一种新型的小胶质细胞Hv(1)通道激活剂，通过未知机制诱导神经炎症。在本研究中，我们利用分子对接、分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟和生物层干涉法（Bio-layer interferometry, BLI）技术，证明了S-023-0515直接结合到Hv(1)通道上。S-023-0515处理诱导了持续的细胞内碱化，导致胞质Ca(2+)水平逐渐升高。主要质膜Ca(2+)离子通道（如TRPV1、Cav1.2、ASIC和P2X7）以及细胞内Ca(2+)释放通道均未参与S-023-0515诱导的Ca(2+)增加。这种Ca(2+)动员通过肌浆/内质网Ca(2+)-ATP酶（SERCA）发生，因为其抑制消除了S-023-0515介导的Ca(2+)升高。Hv(1)介导的Ca(2+)信号进一步促进NF-kappaB激活，导致促炎细胞因子（如TNF-alpha和IL-1beta）在BV-2小胶质细胞中稳定增加，代表一种炎症性小胶质细胞表型。值得注意的是，促炎反应完全归因于Hv(1)通道激活，因为在S-023-0515处理后，NOX2刺激或局部细胞pH值均未改变。总之，这些发现表明，不依赖NOX2的Hv(1)通道激活触发了Hv(1)-SERCA-Ca(2+)-NF-kappaBeta信号级联反应，破坏细胞内Ca(2+)稳态并导致小胶质细胞神经毒性。
